desc: Intro comment header: # List comprehension = A concise way to create lists in Python / Compact and easier to read than traditional loops / [expression for value in iterable if condition]
Traditional loop: doubles = []; for x in range(1, 11): doubles.append(x * 2); print(doubles) -> [2, 4, ..., 20]
doubles = [x * 2 for x in range(1, 11)]; print(doubles) -> [2, 4, ..., 20]
triples = [y * 3 for y in range(1, 11)]; print(triples) -> [3, 6, ..., 30]
squares = [z * z for z in range(1, 11)]; print(squares) -> [1, 4, 9, ..., 100]
fruits = ["apple","orange","banana","coconut"]; fruits = [fruit.upper() for fruit in fruits]; print(fruits) -> ['APPLE','ORANGE','BANANA','COCONUT']
Inline variant: fruits = [fruit.upper() for fruit in ["apple","orange","banana","coconut"]]; print(fruits) (same uppercase output)
fruit_chars = [fruit[0] for fruit in fruits]; print(fruit_chars) -> ['a','o','b','c']
numbers = [1,-2,3,-4,5,-6]; positive_nums = [num for num in numbers if num >= 0]; print -> [1, 3, 5]
negative_nums = [num for num in numbers if num < 0]; print(negative_nums) -> [-2, -4, -6]
even_nums = [num for num in numbers if num % 2 == 0]; print(even_nums) -> [-2, -4, -6]
numbers = [1,-2,3,-4,5,-6,8,-7]; odd_nums = [num for num in numbers if num % 2 == 1]; print(odd_nums) -> [1, 3, 5, -7] (positive/negative/even lines still above)
grades = [85,42,79,90,56,61,30]; passing_grades = [grade for grade in grades if grade >= 60]; print -> [85, 79, 90, 61]
